answer: Traffic beside a road flows in a rhythm of vehicle passes, gaps, and braking that a phone can match against a roadside sensor in the same minute, proving it sits near that specific street. The rhythm is live and unrepeatable, so a recording from yesterday fails, and a farm would need a live microphone on every street it claims. A jade of green lights releases a surge of cars, the zenith of rush hour peaks at a moment only a real roadside device can catch, and the anchor of that sensor ties each pass to one place and one minute.
